scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Pirgousikos originates from the village of Pyrgi (Pirgi) located on the island of Chios in Greece.
Historically, the dance was an integral feature of local community celebrations, particularly during Apokries (the Carnival season preceding Lent) and wedding ceremonies.
Over generations, its musical accompaniment evolved from vocal singing and traditional bagpipe performance to modern violin instrumentation.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Pirgousikos is set to a musical rhythm in 2/4 meter.
Historically, it was performed with dancers singing along, accompanied by the traditional Greek bagpipe known as the tsampouna.
Listen for the Violin, Tsampouna (bagpipe).
The pulse is 2/4.
A crisp, upbeat Aegean instrumental track featuring a prominent lead violin carrying a fast-paced melody in 2/4 meter, historically anchored by the drone and reed sound of the tsampouna bagpipe.
